claims.statement: The claims manual governs internal investigation, evidence preservation, mitigation, valuation, authority, payment, and escalation, but does not create, expand, restrict, or waive insurance coverage; the issued policy and endorsements control coverage decisions.

Property claim handling separates coverage analysis from damage evaluation: the file must establish policy status and applicable terms, investigate cause and scope, preserve evidence, and avoid treating an estimate as proof that the policy responds.

The dwelling-loss workflow requires establishing the efficient cause and sequence of damage, preserving evidence, authorizing only reasonable mitigation, separating direct physical damage from pre-existing or maintenance conditions, and documenting allocation of covered resulting damage before a final coverage position.

Under the HO-3 2024-03 example, accidental discharge or overflow from specified interior systems can cover resulting direct physical loss, while continuous or repeated seepage, loss to the failed system itself, flood or surface water, below-surface water, sump or drainage failure, and defective maintenance or workmanship are separately limited or excluded.

The HO-3 2024-03 example excludes sewer, drain, or sump backup unless a water-backup endorsement is attached, so backup claims require consultation of the attached endorsement rather than assumption from the base form.

The HO 04 27 2016-05 form is an edition-specific limited water-damage endorsement whose coverage and exclusions must be read as issued, including provisions addressing repeated leakage, maintenance, defective work, seepage, and external or drainage-related causes.

The HO 04 90 2027-01 endorsement covers direct physical loss caused by Water Backup or Sump Discharge or Overflow and includes reasonable expenses to prevent further covered damage and remove water within the applicable limit. Its W.2 limit is $10,000 for the loss regardless of the number of insured persons, claims, or covered-property items; coverage remains subject to covered-property, policy-period, and other policy terms, and W.3 provides a $1,000 deductible for each covered water-backup loss.

Water-loss handling requires the adjuster to establish source, path, duration, and prior condition, preserve failed components and claim records, separate emergency mitigation and source repair from resulting damage, and refer external water, backup, freezing, mold, roof leakage, or conflicting-cause issues when the facts or contract require further review.

The HO-3 2024-03 example lists windstorm, hail, falling objects, fire, smoke, and other specified perils, but limits interior rain or snow damage unless wind or hail first creates an opening and excludes cosmetic-only roof-surfacing damage while covering wind or hail damage that impairs water shedding.

Roof claim handling requires inspection and evidence connecting the reported event to physical damage, including roof and interior photographs, weather information, repair history, adjoining-area comparison, and separation of storm-created openings from deterioration, installation defects, prior repairs, and maintenance.

When HO 23 74 2025-05 is attached, roof surfacing aged 12 years or more is settled on an actual-cash-value basis whether or not repaired or replaced; the endorsement uses evidence for the directly damaged portion's roof age, applies the policy limit and deductible, and separately evaluates roof surfacing and other covered property when reasonably possible.

HO 23 74 2025-05 limits roof settlement to supported direct physical damage and like-kind-and-quality repair, while treating matching, detach-and-reset, building requirements, emergency protection, hidden damage, supplements, local pricing, and overhead or profit as fact- and policy-dependent rather than automatic replacement of undamaged surfacing.

Fire and smoke losses require origin, cause, safety, evidence preservation, and recovery review; smoke scope must identify the source and affected components and distinguish smoke residue from ordinary dirt, cooking residue, or pre-existing staining.

Theft handling requires identification of missing property, ownership, location, access, forced-entry facts, timing, and recovery efforts, while vandalism handling requires evidence of intentional damage and separation from accident, neglect, or deterioration; policy-specific vacancy, location, and special-limit terms must then be consulted.

Mold and fungi handling begins with early identification of moisture, intrusion, concealed damage, odor, staining, or growth; it separates microbial damage from the initiating water event and requires the adjuster to connect each testing, cleaning, remediation, repair, or replacement expense to the applicable policy provision.

Loss of use requires a covered direct physical loss that makes the residence unfit for normal use, classification as additional living expense or fair rental value, a supported unfit-for-use date, and coordination of the payment period with necessary repair or replacement; the manual workflow caps additional living expense at 24 months.

Additional living expense is measured as the necessary increase over ordinary household costs and requires reliable records; lodging, meals, transportation, utilities, storage, moving, cleaning, and pet-related expenses are separately reviewed, while ordinary costs, upgrades, luxury accommodations, and discretionary services are excluded from the workflow.

Fair rental value handling requires evidence of an actual rental arrangement and distinguishes rental value from speculative income, repair cost, tenant damage, and business interruption; prolonged displacement, disputed habitability, substantial expense, civil-authority issues, and uncertain repair completion require escalation and duplicate benefits must be avoided.

The claims manual requires referral before settlement or payment when the evaluated loss exceeds $25,000, prohibits dividing activity to avoid authority review, requires approved payment methods and payees, and requires clear explanations for payment, partial payment, or denial.

When HO 04 81 2018-09 is attached, its fungi, wet-rot, dry-rot, and bacteria write-back requires a covered cause to first cause direct physical loss to covered property and the fungi-related loss to result from that loss; the endorsement excludes specified repeated water conditions, flood, preexisting conditions, neglect, maintenance deficiencies, and defective work, and covers remediation-related work only when reasonably necessary and tied to covered direct physical loss.

HO 04 81 2018-09 applies a $10,000 aggregate to all covered fungi, wet-rot, dry-rot, or bacteria loss during the policy term, including covered property damage and related covered expenses across claims, insured persons, and property items; payments reduce the remaining amount, and the applicable deductible is applied only after covered loss is determined.

For Colorado roof-related claim communications, Colorado DOI-2022-08 requires a clear distinction between the coverage determination and the amount offered or paid, and requires disclosure of the settlement method, depreciation or actual-cash-value treatment, distinction between roof surfacing and other property, deductible effect, and material exclusions; its example permits an actual-cash-value roof schedule only when roof age is at least 15 years.

The HO-3 (2024-03) and DP-3 (2026-01) examples exclude earthquake and related earth movement from the base property coverage, so an adjuster must verify a separately issued earthquake policy or endorsement and its covered property, limits, deductible, settlement, and loss-of-use terms before treating earthquake damage as covered.

California CDI-2022-03 controls the offer and administration of earthquake coverage for eligible residential property, requiring a clear written or consented electronic offer that distinguishes earthquake coverage from the underlying policy and identifies material terms, limits, and deductible; the bulletin specifies a 15% seismic deductible of applicable covered loss and treats insured-to-value, replacement-cost settlement, and loss-of-use limits as material terms.

DP-3 Dwelling Property 3 — Special Form (Edition 2026-01) insures direct physical loss to covered property caused by a covered peril subject to the applicable limit and policy period; its Coverage A provision states an 80% amount of insurance and its Coverage B limit is 15% of Coverage A.

Under DP-3 (2026-01), sudden and accidental specified-system water discharge or overflow, fire or lightning, windstorm or hail, and falling objects are listed covered perils, while earth movement, external or below-surface water, repeated seepage, and fungi are excluded; the form can cover resulting direct physical loss while excluding the failed system or excluded condition itself.

DP-3 (2026-01) defines actual cash value as like-kind repair or replacement cost less depreciation and replacement cost without depreciation, settles roof surfacing on an actual-cash-value basis unless HO 23 74 is attached, applies the deductible shown in policy records without stacking deductibles unless required, and limits adjuster communications by prohibiting alteration of coverage, waiver of conditions, or binding beyond authority.
